findings.title: Unbounded raster amplification in PDF ingestion: MuPDF renders the full page surface with no page-count, byte-size or page-dimension cap
findings.description: The render path materializes page rasters proportional to page dimensions inside the vendored MuPDF before any repo-side gate; a measured 819-byte hostile PDF (6000x6000pt MediaBox) produced ~509 MB RSS growth (606x amplification). Remediated by render caps at open.
findings.root_cause: teleocr_engine.render_pages, liteparse_engine._extract_images_sidecar, pdf_local.convert and verify_extraction._source_pages each opened the document with pymupdf.open and handed it straight to rendering/text extraction; MuPDF allocates width x height x 4 bytes per page at render time, and helpers/pdf/ carried no page-count, input-size or page-dimension cap (only post-decode MINIMUM filters: MIN_IMAGE_PX 150, MIN_IMAGE_BYTES 8192, MIN_CHARS_PER_PAGE 100).
findings.intended_behavior: Refuse a document at open, before any page surface is allocated, when it exceeds a page-count cap or a per-page-dimension cap; defaults loud and far above the tracked Reports corpus (200 pages, 4000pt per dimension vs 0.8 MB / 28 A4 pages), overridable per run with --max-pages / --max-page-dims for a document the operator has reviewed.

trace.description: operator-supplied (and via the SEC-6 capture domain, semi-attacker-controlled newsletter imagery) PDF enters the conversion chain
pre-fix: [page.get_pixmap(matrix).tobytes('png') for page in doc] materializes every page's PNG in one eager list, no cap
the vendored parser allocates the uncompressed page surface (width x height x 4 bytes) inside pymupdf, where no Python-side guard can run

evidence.description: pre-fix probe: 819-byte PDF, 2000x2000pt -> 77x amplification; 4000x4000pt -> 275x; 6000x6000pt -> 496 KB pixmap, RSS +509 MB, render 3.47 s (606x), linear in page dimensions
post-fix: the same hostile document is refused by checked_open in 0.6 ms with ~460 KB RSS growth, before any page surface is allocated; A4 28-page fixture passes the defaults unchanged
7 regression tests: dimension cap, count cap, A4 corpus shape passes, teleocr refuses pre-render, CLI flag overrides, flags wired in pdf_conv_md

conditions.description: input PDFs are operator-supplied (Reports/*.pdf) or semi-attacker-controlled via newsletter-embedded imagery captured through the SEC-6 https+magic-byte domain
pre-fix there was no --max-pages / --max-page-dims cap configured anywhere on the conversion chain

execution.attacker_perspective: a tiny hostile PDF (819 bytes) forces the ingestion pipeline to allocate half a gigabyte of raster memory per document, with amplification growing linearly in page dimensions and unbounded relative to input size — a memory-exhaustion lever on the operator's machine reachable through captured newsletter imagery
execution.observed_result: pre-fix: 819 B input, 6000x6000pt MediaBox -> 496 KB pixmap, render 3.47 s, RSS +509 MB (606x); post-fix: RenderLimitExceeded('page 1 is 6000x6000pt, over the 4000pt-per-dimension cap') raised in 0.6 ms with 460 KB RSS growth, no render, through teleocr_engine.render_pages
payloads: 819-byte PDF with a 6000x6000pt MediaBox and one inserted text run (fitz new_page(width=6000, height=6000))
instructions: generate the hostile PDF with fitz (new_page(width=6000, height=6000), one inserted text run)
call helpers.pdf.teleocr_engine.render_pages on it and observe RenderLimitExceeded before any get_pixmap call
rerun pdf_conv_md with --max-page-dims 8000 to see the cap move for a reviewed document

remediation.strategy: render caps at open via one choke point: helpers.pdf.render_limits.checked_open validates page count (MAX_PAGES 200) and per-page dimensions (MAX_PAGE_PTS 4000) before anything renders, closes the document on refusal, and reads the caps as module attributes at call time so the pdf_conv_md CLI flags (--max-pages, --max-page-dims) override them for a reviewed one-off; a refusal is terminal for every engine (no fallback churn) and exits 2 with the flag hint

code_changes.description: new: RenderLimitExceeded + checked_open (page-count and per-page-dimension caps, close-on-refusal, call-time cap reads)
convert() checked_open then pymupdf4llm.to_markdown(doc) in try/finally doc.close() (to_markdown accepts an open Document)
--max-pages/--max-page-dims flags write render_limits.MAX_PAGES/MAX_PAGE_PTS after parse_args; RenderLimitExceeded caught once around the engine chain (stderr hint + exit 2)

likelihood.reason: inputs are operator-supplied Reports or captured newsletter imagery behind the SEC-6 https+magic-byte gate; no unauthenticated network path opens a PDF

impact.reason: measured 606x memory amplification (509 MB from 819 bytes) on the operator machine; exhaustion, not persistence or exfiltration

severity.overall_severity_reason: R1: demonstrated impact is medium (memory exhaustion) but reach is gated through operator-supplied/SEC-6-captured inputs, so overall is bounded at low

confidence.reason: amplification measured on the real render path (three MediaBox sizes, linear scaling confirmed) and the fix demonstrated by the same probe refusing pre-render in 0.6 ms

verification.method: synthetic hostile PDFs through the real render path (fitz-generated MediaBox probes), then the same probe post-fix against checked_open and teleocr_engine.render_pages; no network
verification.observed: pre-fix 606x amplification (RSS +509 MB); post-fix RenderLimitExceeded in 0.6 ms / 460 KB; 11 tests green across render_limits + capture suites
verification.notes: Transport-independent: the allocation is inside vendored MuPDF at render time; the cap operates on document metadata (page count, rect dims) at open, before allocation.
